outcome: A February 2026 preprint (Wang, Wang & Zhou, arXiv:2602.03984) gives a new construction, via equivariant min-max theory, of an embedded non-equatorial minimal hypersphere in S^4, but this is a new proof of a case (n=4, and the ambient even-n cases generally) that was already settled in the negative by Hsiang (and extended by Tomter to all even n) well before the frozen revision date; the genuinely open cases of the problem — odd n≥9 (equivalently even ambient dimension n+1≥10) — are untouched by this or any other work found in the window.

counterexample.object: An embedded non-equatorial minimal hypersphere in S^4 (topologically S^1 x S^2), constructed via equivariant min-max theory
counterexample.verified_how: Variational (min-max) existence proof with regularity theory for the G-equivariant Plateau problem, in a preprint (not yet expert-digested at time of research)

summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet just names 'the spherical Bernstein's problem, a generalization of Bernstein's problem' with no statement of which cases remain open; the problem's own article (checked directly, not the live version but consulted for background as permitted when a nested/linked article is needed to make sense of the bullet) explains that Chern's problem asks whether equators are the only smooth embedded minimal hyperspheres in S^(n+1), that n=3 was resolved by Almgren-Calabi, that Hsiang resolved it negatively for n in {4,5,6,7,8,10,12,14}, and that Tomter (1987) extended the negative resolution to all even n -- leaving it open only for odd n>=9 (equivalently even ambient dimension n+1>=10). This matches the triage's own summary of the state of the art. The one item found in the window, arXiv:2602.03984 (Wang, Wang & Zhou, submitted February 2026, revised August 2026), gives a new min-max-theoretic construction of a non-equatorial minimal hypersphere in S^4 specifically, calling it 'a new resolution of Chern's spherical Bernstein problem in S^4.' Since S^4 (n=4, even) was already settled in the negative by Hsiang decades before the 26 January 2024 snapshot, this is a new proof technique for an already-closed case, not new territory, so it is dated 'open_stale' with respect to the genuinely open cases (odd n>=9 / even ambient n+1>=8+2). I found no work in the window that touches the actually-open odd-n>=9 cases: searches for progress there surfaced only work on the superficially similarly-named but distinct 'stable Bernstein problem' (Chodosh-Li 2023-2024, Chodosh-Li-Minter-Stryker 2026, Mazet 2024), which is a different problem about stability of minimal hypersurfaces in Euclidean space, not Chern's spherical Bernstein problem, and was correctly not conflated here. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the 2602.03984 preprint's methods, acknowledgements, or in secondary discussion found; the work uses purely classical equivariant min-max variational methods.
competing_reading: One could argue the new 2602.03984 construction, even though S^4 was already known to admit non-equatorial minimal hyperspheres, still counts as 'progress' because it introduces a new equivariant min-max machinery (regularity theory for the G-equivariant Plateau/isotopy problem in manifolds with 3-dimensional orbit space) that the authors may intend to extend to the genuinely open odd n>=9 cases -- the triage's `why` field raises exactly this possibility. However, the paper itself only claims the S^4 result; no extension to higher/open dimensions is proved or even conjectured concretely in the version I reviewed, so I did not classify this as `progress` on the open cases. If a follow-up paper by the same or other authors applies this machinery to an open dimension, that would change the classification.
what_would_settle_it: A paper (from these or other authors) that applies equivariant min-max theory, or any other technique, to construct or rule out a non-equatorial minimal hypersphere for some odd n>=9 (or even ambient dimension n+1>=10), which is the actual open frontier of the problem.
